🤭How to make money online selling products on Etsy you didn't make yourself using the done for you designs & print on demand method!  👇🏼Read for a step by step!  🙌🏼 How Print On Demand Works:  1. Do Some Quick Product Research - Look for popular items people are buying, like wall art, t-shirts, sweatshirts, phone cases, candles, mugs, or tote bags.   - Use tools like erank, Google Trends or browse online shops to see what's trending. I also look for inspo on Pinterest all the time! I like to use Everbee to see how much money a product is making on Etsy.  2. Create Your Design  - Get done for you designs on ctrl-alt-design.com  - Or create your own. Make your design fun, eye-catching, or niche-specific. Keep it simple and high-quality!   3. Sign Up on Printify  - Create a free account & make sure you connect your account to a store. Examples being Etsy or Shopify. You are walked through how to do this when you sign up, don’t worry it’s easy and fast.  4. Choose a Product on Printify   - Browse the product catalog for posters, t-shirts, hoodies, candles, hats, mugs, phone cases & etc.   - Select the product you want to sell.   5. Upload Your Design   - Click on the product to customize it.   - Upload your design.   - Position and resize it to fit the product nicely.   6. Fill Out Listing Details  - Write a catchy product title and description with keywords.   - Set your price (consider costs and your profit margin).   7. Publish Your Product  - Remember to connect your online store (Shopify, Etsy, etc.) with Printful . This makes it so whenever you make a sale, Printify knows instantly so it can print the design on the product for you and send it to the customer for you!  - Publish your product so it’s live and ready for customers.   8. Market Your Product - Share your product on social media, use Pinterest, create ads, or tell friends. Make videos of your product or make Pinterest pins.  - Focus on your target audience to attract more buyers. Not a must but it can help!  #howtomakemoneyonline #sidehustle #onlinesidehustle #printondemand #digitalproducts

Ethical platforms to use instead of Etsy. Here are 7 ethical alternatives people are switching to. Artisans Cooperative. Owned by its makers and shoppers, one vote per member, with the community verifying shops are handmade. Folksy. It bans resellers and mass-produced imports, and makers get paid directly. Handfair. One owner, no investors, makers keep 100% of the item price, and it blocks AI from training on their work. Mayhem Marketplace. It charges a flat subscription instead of taking a cut of every sale, and it bans dropshipping and products made mainly by AI. Marmalade. A small team that checks the handmade shops it promotes. No AI, no dropshipping. Big Cartel. Independent since 2005, no commission, and a free plan. Wolf & Badger. A certified B Corp marketplace where every brand is owned by its designer. Starting December 16, Etsy and its partners can use sellers' photos and descriptions to train AI. Sellers can't just turn it off in their settings. Artists are already pulling their shops. Over the years, Etsy started allowing factory-made goods, went public, dropped its B Corp certification, and now answers to shareholders before its users. Buyers say the site is filled with junk. Etsy is rated a D on the Conscious Spend app, where we are on a mission to show consumers how ethical almost any company is so people can find ethical alternatives to evil corporations. You can also use the app to see who owns what you buy, better alternatives, and the ethics score, and join over 125k people using it to spend for a better world.

videos.caption: 💔 Etsy Shop Announcement Video 😭 • • I put on my story the other day that I would be making an announcement regarding my Etsy shop and here it is. Etsy has decided to make a new policy that would make it so that they could take any listing image up on their page (starting on Dec. 16th) and take it to train AI. I think it’s absolutely ridiculous that Etsy is doing this, especially since SO many artists use their site to host their shop. Ever since I heard the news, I knew I had to make the unfortunate decision to close my shop (which sucks because I haven’t even had it open for a year yet!). If anyone has any suggestions for where to host my shop, I would super appreciate it! And if you could help support me and my shop that would be super appreciated as well! I will be having a sale from Nov. 8th-Dec. 15th (and on Dec. 15th I will be closing my shop for good).
